key_insight: Time-lagged cross-correlation (TCC) ranks existing flow modes by their association with a target observable, revealing relevant structures that global contribution rankings can miss.
engineering_relevance: Observable-specific mode selection helps identify flow structures associated with engineering quantities such as lift and drag without changing the underlying modal expansion.
method: Start with a fixed DMD or POD expansion, preserving spatial modes and temporal coefficients.
Rank mode groups by the mean squared norm of their cross-responses with the target over a lag window.
Select target-related structures; for POD, this minimises weighted correlation-operator truncation error among equally sized subsets.
evidence_signal: Tests on synthetic flow, a cylinder wake, and a cavity recovered observable-related structures, with 2.15% target-subfield reconstruction error in the synthetic case.
watch_item: Benefits of lag aggregation depend on the cross-response distribution and lag-window selection, and selection remains constrained to the existing modal basis.
paper_title: Extracting target-related flow structures using a time-lagged cross-correlation ranking criterion
